newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria hopes reforms will boost EBRD investment.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria hopes reforms will boost EBRD investment.

text.p: Bulgaria hopes that radical reforms pledged by its interim cabinet will improve the business climate and boost investment by the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development, a senior central banker said.

"With the latest news of approved international funding Bulgarian investment prospects have improved and there are chances of speeding up EBRD projects planned for this year," central bank deputy governor Plamen Ilchev told Reuters.

At the annual meeting of the EBRD next week in London, Ilchev hopes to promote investment possibilities to portfolio investors in Bulgarian external and dometic debt instruments, and the bank's participation in sell-offs of major state firms.

"There are real chances for the EBRD to participate in the privatisation of major chemical and cement state-owned plants, either as an additional investor or with medium-term funding for technological upgrade," said Ilchev.
"Now that privatisation seems to be speeding up, many of these projects can be completed sooner," said Ilchev, who is also Bulgaria's governor for the EBRD.
He said the bank planned to invest in the biggest regional soda ash producer Sodi-Devnya, after its sale to Belgian chemical group Solvay SA is finalised.
The EBRD also plans to participate in the privatisation of the United Bulgarian Bank, with some 24 million Ecus along with another investor.
The bank revised its funding strategy for Bulgaria last year after delayed reforms deterred development of the private sector.

Delayed structural reform, a weak and poorly functioning banking system, corruption and slow and reluctant privatisation mean Bulgaria has failed to meet a 60/40 private/public portfolio requirement which is due in June 1997.

The EBRD has so far approved 21 investments totalling 215.5 million European Currency Units in the financial sector, agribusiness, transportation, telecommunications, energy insurance and consumer goods.
Eighteen percent of the signed projects are in the private sector.

Earlier this year the EBRD said there were projects in the pipeline which could result in EBRD committing between $100 million and $200 million once the government signs an agreement with the International Monetary Fund.
A $659 million funding package agreed with the IMF on March 17 paved the way to winning additional support of some $400 million from European Union and the Group of 24 richest countries this week.

Bulgaria now has a serious chance of successfully implementing a currency board regime, restoring confidence in its troubled financial system and laying the foundation for economic recovery, President Petar Stoyanov said on Thursday.

The caretaker government says it has fulfilled pledges to the IMF to prepare the implementation of the currency board system by the new government and parliament after April 19 elections. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
